Electric Utilities Industry in Vietnam Posts Stable Trade Figures Amid Steady Demand

The electric utilities sector in Vietnam reported steady trade figures for the first quarter of the year, reflecting consistent demand growth and ongoing infrastructure investments across the country. According to data released by the Vietnam Electric Utilities Association (VEUA) on Thursday, total electricity output for the period reached 62.3 billion kilowatt-hours, a 4.2% increase compared to the same period last year.

Export activity in the sector remained limited but stable, with neighboring Laos and Cambodia continuing to be the main recipients of Vietnamese electricity exports. The VEUA reported that cross-border electricity sales amounted to 1.1 billion kilowatt-hours, in line with figures from previous quarters.

“Vietnam’s electric utilities industry continues to benefit from both strong domestic demand and stable regional trade relationships,” said Nguyen Van Hoa, director of market analysis at the VEUA. “Growth is driven primarily by ongoing industrialization and rising household consumption, particularly in urban centers such as Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi.”

Imports of equipment and technology used for power generation and grid expansion also remained consistent. The Ministry of Industry and Trade reported that Vietnam imported $278 million worth of electrical machinery and components in the first quarter, slightly above last year’s figure. These imports are largely destined for ongoing projects aimed at modernizing the national grid and integrating more renewable energy sources.

Nguyen Thi Lan, spokesperson for Dong Nam Electric, a major industry player, highlighted the sector’s focus on reliability and service quality. “Routine maintenance and incremental upgrades are ensuring we meet the growing needs of businesses and consumers,” she said. “We are investing in both transmission infrastructure and customer service to maintain stable supplies.”

Industry analysts noted that the sector’s performance reflects the broader stability of Vietnam’s economy, which continues to post positive growth rates despite global uncertainties. “As long as manufacturing and urbanization trends persist, we expect steady, incremental gains in the electric utilities sector,” said Truong Minh Phuc, an energy consultant at Indochina Market Advisory.

The VEUA expects electricity consumption to continue rising in the coming months, in line with seasonal patterns and ongoing economic expansion. No major changes in trade policy or industry regulation are anticipated for the remainder of the year.
